clue.text: What dog did to cat, say, is not spotted at all

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a dog runs after a cat, so it chased it

explanation.surface: A dog went after the cat, yet the cat came through without a mark on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspotted is an old sense of pure and virtuous, without moral stain, which is what chaste means.

clue.text: Ready for card-carrying customers?

parts.note: ready is slang for money, and shoppers paying by debit card can ask the till for some money to be handed over with their purchase

explanation.surface: A shop declares itself prepared to serve people who carry membership cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective meaning prepared; here it is the noun 'readies', slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket service gives debit-card users banknotes at the till, which is ready money for card holders.

clue.text: Drink said to make one feel unwell

indicators.note: said tells us the drink's name is to be spoken, not written

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drink is supposed to give you a queasy feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict someone with sickness, making them unwell.

clue.text: Aim to deceive sea-god, grabbing fishy tail

indicators.note: grabbing means the sea-god's name holds another letter within it

parts.note: Triton is the merman god of the sea in Greek myth

indicators.note: tail means only the end letter of the word fishy is used

explanation.surface: Someone plots to trick a god of the sea who has seized a fish by its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for attempting to get away with a deception or cheek.

clue.text: In response to prayer, expert is prepared to listen

parts.note: amen is said by a congregation at the end of a prayer
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: After someone says a prayer, a skilled person shows willingness to hear them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is open to suggestion and willing to listen to reason, a close synonym.

clue.text: Henry Ford's brainchild —- show support for state of America

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits under the first, so it is a support for it

parts.note: Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state
a production is a staged show

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on a show backing a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford's assembly line in the early 20th century is the standard example of making goods in huge numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford pioneered the moving assembly line, the founding example of making identical goods in huge quantities.

clue.text: Endless new work's just about on the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: just about means almost all, so the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work, so work's gives OPS

explanation.surface: A new piece of work is nearly ready and on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' looks like wordplay asking you to cut letters off; it is the definition, meaning without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-stop goes on without any break, so it seems to have no end.

clue.text: Drunken don grabbing literary giants here

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy university lecturer seizes hold of famous writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary giants' sounds like great authors, but it means real giants in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift's Gulliver's Travels, the land of giants is the place Gulliver visits on his second voyage.

clue.text: Owner of kayak, one at bottom of river a short time

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece at the bottom of another comes after it

parts.note: the Esk is a river in northern England and Scotland
I is the Roman numeral one
mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: Someone who owns a canoe sits at the bottom of a river for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The kayak is the traditional skin boat of the Arctic peoples formerly called by this name.

clue.text: It's simple to prepare, if you're patient

definitions.text: It's simple to prepare, if you're patient

parts.words: It's simple to prepare, if you're patient
parts.note: simple is an old noun for a medicinal plant, and patient is a sick person rather than someone calm

explanation.surface: Advice that something is easy to make as long as you take your time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' reads as easy and 'patient' as unhurried; really a simple is a healing plant and a patient is someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy brewed from healing plants, the old simples, is prepared for someone who is ill.

clue.text: Start off daily lessons in convulsions when frivolous reports are read

indicators.note: in convulsions shows the letters being thrown about into a new order
start off means the first letter of the word daily is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut the daily classes while doubled up with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops D from DAILY, leaving AILY; that and LESSONS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: British newspapers call late summer, when little serious news happens, the time for trivial stories.

clue.text: Yob in Grease finally a changed character

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: oil is grease, a lubricant

explanation.surface: A hooligan in the musical Grease ends up a reformed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grease' looks like the musical; it is simply OIL, whose final L becomes K.
explanation.definitionFit: Oik is British slang for an uncouth or loutish person, much like yob.

clue.text: Film made by soap in this city bar recalled

definitions.text: Film made by soap in this

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: recalled means the word is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: but means except, as does bar

explanation.surface: A film shot about a soap opera in a city pub is called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' and 'soap' suggest cinema and TV; it is a scummy layer left by soap in a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is the vessel in which soap leaves a scummy film or ring.

clue.text: Grand spot? It might be, for general store

indicators.note: might be hints that the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A great location could make a good village shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading post is a frontier shop selling all manner of goods, a general store.

clue.text: Very keen to pack in going round where conference was held

indicators.note: going round means the whole run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: mad as in mad about, very keen
to pack in is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone so eager they cannot give up going around.
explanation.walkthrough: Both MAD and STOP are reversed together, giving the letters in the order shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allied leaders met in this town near Berlin in 1945 to settle post-war Germany.

clue.text: Activity of couch potato or booze cruiser?

definitions.meaning: a lazy TV watcher flicks repeatedly between stations with the remote
British shoppers who cross to France for cheap alcohol go back and forth across the English Channel

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses involve switching channels: TV stations by remote, or the sea strait between England and France by ferry.

clue.text: Panic originally associated say with their letters

indicators.note: the letters are put together in an arrangement different from the original
letters invites us to use the letters of the words themselves, rearranged

explanation.surface: A panic once linked, so to speak, with their correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the Greek origin of the word, once associated with the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled emotional excess, a state of wild panic.

clue.text: Mark's successor perhaps attains popularity after forty-five?

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first

parts.note: a 45 is a single record played at 45 rpm
currency can mean general acceptance or popularity

explanation.surface: A man named Mark's heir becomes popular after the age of forty-five.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is the Deutschmark, replaced by the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro replaced the German mark as one shared money for many countries, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Got the picture from file Guardian's foremost journalist kept

indicators.note: kept means the first pieces hold the file inside them
foremost means take only the first letter of the newspaper's name

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: A reporter at the Guardian understood a photo from the archive.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the picture is an idiom for understanding, which is what grasped means here.

clue.text: Bitter resentment that's expressed in private

indicators.note: expressed means put into speech, so we hear a soundalike

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier serving in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: Deep bitterness is voiced only behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In private' looks like 'secretly'; private is the lowest army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is long-held bitter ill will, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Be in dispute with bank in town at start of March

parts.note: to jar is to clash or disagree
a row is a bank or tier, as of seats or keys

explanation.surface: Arguing over a riverbank in a town at the beginning of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1936 Jarrow March saw unemployed men from this Tyneside town walk to London.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1936 hunger march to London set off from this north-east English town.

clue.text: A sequence of letters with article written in Pashto

indicators.note: written in means the article goes inside the run of letters

parts.note: F, G, H, I is a run of consecutive letters of the alphabet
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A string of characters with a piece in a newspaper printed in an Afghan language.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is the main language of Afghanistan, loosely called by the country's adjective.

clue.text: Mean to keep working this evening

indicators.note: to keep means the stingy word holds the other inside it

parts.note: tight means mean with money
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A plan to carry on working later today.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of today, this evening.

clue.text: Animal requiring a lot of space

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: room is space

explanation.surface: A creature that needs plenty of room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is a common Australian shortening for kangaroo, an animal.

clue.text: Bacon, for instance, that's poor sorted out with his help

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters are rearranged into proper order

explanation.surface: A struggling Francis Bacon gets his finances put right with help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' could be the meat or the painter; here it is Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English thinker who founded empiricism, an example of a deep thinker.

clue.text: The shot to beat —- a winner

definitions.meaning: to beat someone is to strike them
a success, such as a chart-topping song, is called a smash

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a blow on target, the verb to strike, and a popular success.

clue.text: Scratched and picked

parts.note: with means together with, and
drew as in drew lots, picked

explanation.surface: Something was scraped and then chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' looks like scraped; in racing a scratched horse is one pulled out before the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who is scratched is pulled out of a race, which means withdrew.

clue.text: Decay found in vegetable or shrub

indicators.note: found in means one word sits inside another

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
rot is decay

explanation.surface: Rot discovered in a vegetable or a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a South African flowering shrub.
